title: bug: postflight-worktree.cjs wt-resume pins neither half of the L2 marker-scan union, so three sh mutants of the completion's conflict check survive
description:
Problem: at a worktree completion, L2's marker check scans the union of `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` (unmerged paths) and `task.landingRetry.paths`. It scans whenever landingRetry is set, not only while MERGE_HEAD exists, and a marker left is MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT. The wt-resume chain in scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs has exactly one conflict path, src/a.txt, which is both a retry path and unmerged. So no case pins either half of the union, or the trigger, on its own.

Evidence: QA comment-cf8ade2050f840a3bb2d6b15b0a05787 on task-b1ca54f2 (WT-19), from the WT-11 review (task-dd1ee586, approved at 7cd8e423). Three sh mutants survived the wt-resume case: (1) dropping the `--diff-filter=U` half of the union; (2) dropping the landingRetry.paths half; (3) scanning only while MERGE_HEAD exists. The mutant driver is D:\moe-scratch\qa-wt11\mut\run.sh, with details in Serena memory decision-worktree-pending-merge-checkpoint. The production code for all three is present and correct by inspection, so this is a test gap, not a wrapper defect.

Impact: a later edit that drops either half, or narrows the trigger, passes the suite. A completion could then land conflict markers on the target: markers left on a path outside landingRetry.paths, or a retry path's markers after `merge --quit` has removed MERGE_HEAD.

Fix: add two cases to postflight-worktree.cjs and run each in both engines (sh and ps1):
(a) a resume whose merge conflicts on a path outside landingRetry.paths; a completion that leaves markers there prints MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT, lands nothing and routes conflict;
(b) markers left in a landingRetry path with no MERGE_HEAD; the completion also refuses.
Prove each case kills its mutant: temporarily apply the mutant, see the case fail, then restore. Test files only; no wrapper change unless a case exposes a real defect, which then gets its own row.
definitionOfDone: postflight-worktree.cjs has case (a): a conflict on a path outside landingRetry.paths, with markers left at completion, gives MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT, nothing lands, and the route is conflict, on both the sh and ps1 engines
postflight-worktree.cjs has case (b): markers in a landingRetry path with no MERGE_HEAD refuse the completion the same way, on both engines
Each of the three mutants named in the description fails at least one new case (record the RED runs), and the restored wrapper passes
node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash and postflight-safe.mjs powershell (Windows node) pass, with counts recorded; bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes
No assertion in an existing case is weakened, and scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} are unchanged
reopenReason: Governor promote under the human's standing "move from backlog" (2026-11-02 21:00Z). This is a worker-filed WT-19 adversarial finding: a test-only gap in scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs, evidenced by QA comment-cf8ade20 on task-b1ca54f2. It has no dependencies, and 3 coders are idle. The human can drag it back to veto.

comments.content:
Governor note for the planner. The HIGH task-e3e81c45 (Serena ignore override, WORKING and gated on c6a24053) also plans new cases in scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs.
- No dependsOn edge: in worktree mode an overlap on a shared file lands by merge-tree, and WT-19's DoD 3 sweep drops file-only edges.
- To keep the two landings from colliding, put cases (a) and (b) in their own block beside the existing wt-resume chain, not at the end of the file or the end of the case table, and edit with the Edit tool.
- If the landing still conflicts, the conflict-resume path takes it back to the worker; don't serialize the rows ahead of time.
- Keep the description's limits: scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} unchanged, no existing assertion weakened, and each mutant's RED run recorded.
